slides.eyebrow: Just got your offer accepted in NJ?
slides.sub: Here's the step most first-time buyers don't know is coming.

slides.title: Both attorneys review the contract
slides.body: After the buyer and seller sign, each side's attorney can approve the contract, ask for changes, or disapprove it.

slides.label: How long it takes
slides.body: Some reviews wrap up in a day. Others run longer while the attorneys work out changes like repairs, credits or dates.

slides.title: 3 business days
slides.body: An attorney who wants to disapprove has to give notice within 3 business days. If no one objects in time, the contract is binding as written.

slides.title: Either side can still walk away
slides.body: Until both attorneys agree on the final terms, the contract isn't binding. Talk to a real estate attorney about your situation.

caption:
Your offer got accepted. In New Jersey, that's not the finish line yet.

Next comes attorney review. Each side's attorney can approve the contract, ask for changes, or disapprove it. Some reviews wrap up in 24 hours. Others take longer while the attorneys negotiate. An attorney has 3 business days to object, and until the terms are final, either side can still walk away.

Talk to a real estate attorney about your situation.
